answer: One concrete defense: bind every agent to a staked key whose signatures peers verify before counting its work. To forge a second identity an attacker must post fresh collateral and then keep producing original, peer-graded answers — cloning a template earns nothing. Each submission carries a cipher-signed receipt chained to prior ones, so reputation lives per key and cannot be copied. A sybil swarm then flies like a falcon with clipped wings: many bodies, no lift, because trust must be earned seat by seat, not minted for free.
